'''Mirza Abdul Baqi Bég''' (20 September 1934 – 30 January 1990), also known as '''MAB Bég''' or '''Baqi Bég''', was a [[Pakistanis|Pakistani]] [[Theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]] and a professor of physics at the [[Rockefeller University]] whose contributions were vital in [[string theory]] and [[particle physics]].<ref name="World Scientific, Hoodbhoy & Ali">{{cite book |last1=A |first1=Ali |last2=Pervez |first2=Hoodbhoy |authorlink2=Pervez Hoodbhoy |title=MAB Beg Memorial Volume |date=1991 |publisher=World Scientific |location=New Jersey, U.S. |isbn=978-981-4555-96-8 |pages=290 |edition=1st |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=0IcvDwAAQBAJ |accessdate=29 April 2020 |language=en-us |format=google books}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.nytimes.com/1990/02/01/obituaries/mirza-abdul-beg-55-a-professor-of-physics.html |title = Mirza Abdul Beg, 55, A Professor of Physics|newspaper = The New York Times|date = February 1990}}</ref>
He is mainly known for his role in laying down the theoretical foundations of the [[quark]] theory as well as developing the [[SU(6)]] model.<ref>[http://lib-docs.web.cern.ch/lib-docs/Archives/biographies/Beg_MAB-199205.pdf Biography] cern.ch</ref>

==Biography==
Bég was born in [[Etawah]], [[Uttar Pradesh]] in [[British Indian Empire|India]] on 20 September 1934.{{rp|xv}}<ref name="World Scientific, Hoodbhoy & Ali"/> Following the [[Partition of India|partition]] of India in 1947, his family migrated to Pakistan, only to be settled in [[Karachi]], [[Sindh]], [[Pakistan]].{{rp|xv}}<ref name="World Scientific, Hoodbhoy & Ali"/> After finishing school in Karachi, Bég went to attend the [[University of Sindh]] in [[Hyderabad, Pakistan|Hyderabad]], graduated with [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] with honors in [[Physics]] in 1951.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ensf-ngo.org/new/mab.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=2017-03-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304202340/http://www.ensf-ngo.org/new/mab.pdf |archive-date=2016-03-04 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Upon returning to Karachi, Bég attended the [[Karachi University]] where he graduated with his [[Master of Science|MSc]] in [[Mathematics]] with area focused on the [[Applied Mathematics|applied application]] in 1954.{{rp|xvi}}<ref name="World Scientific, Hoodbhoy & Ali"/>  Bég went to [[United States]] for his doctoral studies, attending the [[University of Pittsburgh]], where he was conferred with [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in nuclear physics under Dr. Philip M. Stehl in 1958.<ref>{{cite web |title=Mirza A. B. Beg {{!}} Physics & Astronomy {{!}} University of Pittsburgh |url=https://www.physicsandastronomy.pitt.edu/people/mirza-b-beg |website=www.physicsandastronomy.pitt.edu |accessdate=29 April 2020}}</ref>

Before moving to [[England]], Bég's early work was focused toward [[nuclear physics]], and got interested in theoretical physics after accepting his postdoctoral fellowship (1958-1960) at the [[University of Birmingham]], working under Sir [[Rudolf Peierls]] at the department of physics, followed by his second post-doc at the [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]] at [[Upton, New York|Upton]], [[New York (state)|New York]]. His work at BNL earned him a membership at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in Princeton, New Jersey (1962–64), where he spent two highly-productive years in developing the foundations of valuable work he later carried out.

He joined the faculty of physics at the [[Rockefeller University]] in 1964 and was promoted to full Professor in 1968. Soon after his appointment, beginning with 1965 he became a consultant at the [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]] (serving on its High Energy Advisory Committee from 1975 to 1978, which took decisions on the selection of experiments to be conducted at the laboratory.) He also contributed significantly to other global particle physics endeavors, most notably, at the [[Stanford Linear Accelerator Center]] and at the [[European Organization for Nuclear Research]]. He was appointed as a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] and the [[New York Academy of Sciences]], in addition to recognition by the [[American Institute of Physics]].<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.aip.org/history-programs/niels-bohr-library/photos/beg-mirza-a1 | title=Portrait of Beg Beg Mirza A1| date=2014-02-24}}</ref>

Beg made a number of contributions to the then pioneering efforts in the structure of elementary particles and the development of the [[quark]] theory, especially contributing to the important symmetries in physics which underlie our understanding of the elementary particles. His important work lies in the domain of [[group theory]], especially in the [[SU(6)]] model. He was a driving force and inspiration for generations of particle physicists.{{Citation needed|date= May 2022}}

Beg was a bona fide and valuable citizen scientist and believed in science as a tool for human development and uplift. "He held the view that science, in particular fundamental science, is the best catalyst for inducing far reaching socio-political changes in contemporary societies and that it provides a universal opportunity to make a lasting contribution to human knowledge.", based on which The Emerging Nations Science Foundation (ESNF), a non-governmental organization based in Trieste, Italy, has constituted a prize in his memory, named the "ENSF Prize in Physics (In memoriam M.A.B. Beg)".<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ensf-ngo.org/new/prizes.php |title=The Emerging Nations Science Foundation |access-date=2017-03-04 |archive-date=2017-04-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170430105455/http://www.ensf-ngo.org/new/prizes.php |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He died peacefully at his home in Manhattan, New York, on 30 January 1990, survived by his wife Nancie.{{Citation needed|date= May 2022}} An obituary was published in [[New York Times]] on 1 February 1990.{{Citation needed|date= May 2022}}

A memorial was published in his memory (widely known as The "M.A.B. Beg Memorial Volume") in 1991 by World Scientific, which includes several papers written by him as well as other prominent particle physicists.<ref>{{cite book | last=Ali | first=A. | last2=Hoodbhoy | first2=P. | title=M.a.b. Beg Memorial Volume | publisher=World Scientific Publishing Company | year=1991 | isbn=978-981-4555-96-8 | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=0IcvDwAAQBAJ}}</ref>
